topic: Touch screen interaction and UI design

summary.goal: Provide guidelines for designing usable, accessible, and device-adapted touch interfaces

format.name: The right format
rules: Validate screen size, resolution, and orientation early
Use responsive design for web interfaces
Consider non-standard formats for devices like kiosks and wearables
Account for haptic resolution when designing touch targets
format.design_intent: Ensure UI adapts correctly to physical and technical constraints

size_and_spacing.name: Spacings and size
rules: Minimum touch target: ~1 cm (≈44px, device dependent)
Increase spacing between interactive elements
Adapt spacing for lower-quality or large displays
Avoid dense layouts that increase tap errors
size_and_spacing.design_intent: Prevent accidental taps and improve interaction accuracy

placement.name: Placement
rules: Avoid covering important content with hands
Minimize movement effort (especially on large screens)
Place frequently used controls within easy reach
Consider top vs bottom navigation depending on context

gestures.name: Gestures
rules: Use standard gestures whenever possible
Avoid conflicts with OS/system gestures
Provide visual/animated affordances for gestures
Provide accessibility alternatives (e.g., tap instead of drag)

keyboard.name: Keyboards
rules: Display the correct keyboard type (text, numeric, etc.)
Ensure inputs are visible when keyboard is open
Prevent input fields from being obscured

privacy.name: Privacy
rules: Limit personal data requests
Be cautious with large/public displays where content is visible at distance
privacy.design_intent: Protect user data in exposed environments

principles: Provide single-tap alternatives for complex gestures
Ensure sufficient touch area and spacing
Avoid reliance on precise motor control
Support visibility under different viewing angles

components: buttons must meet minimum target size
lists must include adequate vertical spacing
navigation should adapt to device ergonomics
interaction_patterns: prefer tap over drag for critical actions
